filter.comment: Episode = take = ego mp4 (e.g. P01-20240202-110250); 156 takes across P01-P09. take id = mp4 basename = video_id in the narrations = gaze-dir stem inside mps_<takeid>_vrs.

params.scale_to_mp4: multiply output px by mp4_width/2880 (ffprobe mp4 W per take)
params.out_of_fov: fn returns None outside FOV -> null gaze for that frame

projection.time_sync: Same Aria scheme as nymeria: device_ts_us(frame i) = first_gaze_ts_us + round(i*1e6/mp4_fps). ffprobe mp4 fps per take. Validate frame-0 anchor vs Videos/<P##>/<takeid>_mp4_to_vrs_time_ns.csv (per-frame mp4->vrs ns map) which gives the exact mp4-frame device timestamps for hd-epic (unlike nymeria).
projection.notes: Identical Aria MPS to nymeria (general only; no personalized). Calibration is NOT under GAZE_HAND: deref SLAM/multi/vrs_to_multi_slam.json -> index N. hd-epic ALSO ships Videos/<P##>/<takeid>_mp4_to_vrs_time_ns.csv (per-frame mp4<->vrs timestamp map) -> use it for exact frame timing rather than inferring. Apply the nymeria-validated projection params (make_upright=true, scale by mp4_w/2880, per-sample depth_m).

join.comment: DataFrame columns: unique_narration_id, participant_id, video_id, narration, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, nouns, verbs, pairs, main_actions, *_classes, hands, narration_timestamp. Rows where video_id == episode id. start/end are float seconds. main_actions is list-valued (preserve as extra).

anchor.detail: Videos/<P##>/<takeid>_mp4_to_vrs_time_ns.csv gives exact per-frame mp4<->device(vrs) ns; use it for the anchor. Fallback: first_gaze_sample (gaze t0=50.44, span 396.2s == video 396.3s).

annotations.note: HD_EPIC narration start/end_timestamp are already video-zero seconds (7.4-394.7 within video 396.3)

epoch_sync.verified: gaze rebased span 396.2s vs video 396.27s; anno 7.44-394.72 already video-zero

metadata.notes: frames.txt gives per-mp4 frame count (duration.txt named in readme is absent). fps inferred ~30 (Aria RGB) but not on-disk-confirmed; ffprobe at metadata time. HD_EPIC_{verb,noun}_classes.csv map class ids -> canonical key+category (not required for text channel). The .pkl is the ONLY copy of narrations (no CSV sibling) -> pandas required to read it.

provenance.notes: METADATA none, readme.txt at root. VIDEO Videos/P0<k>/. GAZE SLAM-and-Gaze/P0<k>/GAZE_HAND/<take>/eye_gaze/general_eye_gaze.csv (not pixel-mapped; process like nymeria). ANNOTATION narrations-and-action-segments/HD_EPIC_Narrations.pkl (extract narration, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, main_actions).
decisions: Episode = take/ego mp4 (156); gaze dir = mps_<takeid>_vrs; narration join by video_id.
Gaze = Aria CPF (general only); preserve full CPF columns; project via projectaria_tools.
Single annotation channel 'narration' (intervals, text=narration); preserve main_actions + verbs/nouns/pairs as extras.
Apply the erratum denylist (55 ids) to drop corrected narrations.
corrections: Calibration is under SLAM/multi/<N>/ (deref vrs_to_multi_slam.json), NOT co-located under GAZE_HAND as in nymeria.
Narration timestamps are float SECONDS, not HH:MM:SS strings.
The narrations .pkl is the only copy (pandas-only); no CSV sibling exists.
duration.txt (per readme) is absent; only frames.txt present.
No VRS files in this deposit.
open_questions: main_actions exact container (list vs ndarray vs delimited) and per-row float timestamps need pandas to materialize (could not confirm cell encodings without pandas on remote).
fps not confirmed on-disk (no ffprobe); validate via ffprobe + frames.txt.
No official train/val/test split on disk; source externally if needed.
